5. Take education=10 in Eq.1, we can get wage[ = 57405.06 + 17910.03 × 10 = 236505.36.

6. R2 = 0.1225, which means 12.25% of the sample variation in wages is explained by

8. SLR.4 is E(µi|educationi) = 0, which implies that an individual’s year of education is
   uncorrelated with any unobservable factors.

   It doesn’t hold because one’s education level might be correlated with his ability, in-

   model.
